title: Adaptive cohort-based A/B runner with early-stop & safety gates for model versions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams need a safe, auditable way to compare model versions in production while limiting customer exposure and enabling automatic rollback when safety or quality regressions appear. Current A/B tools are either too coarse (global traffic split) or manual (engineers patch routing and watch dashboards).

Goal: Build an A/B experiment runner that: (1) supports stratified cohorts (by region, customer tier, route), (2) performs sequential statistical checks with early-stop and Bayesian checks, (3) exposes staged ramping and shadowing controls, and (4) supports automatic rollback / pause when pre-defined guardrails are violated. The runner must integrate with Console and the routing layer and produce explainable audit logs for compliance.
acceptance_criteria:
- PM and Eng sign-off on experiment config schema and UI.
- Console UI allows creation of cohort-based experiments with at least three stratification dimensions (region, plan, endpoint).
- Routing honors cohort allocations; shadow traffic option forwards requests to candidate without affecting responses.
- Statistical engine runs continuous checks and surfaces decisions (pass/fail/insufficient-data).
- Auto-rollback triggers when any high-priority guardrail breaches for 3 consecutive intervals.
- Audit log contains experiment decisions, metric snapshots, and action timestamps.
- Load tests show experiment coordinator adds <5% CPU overhead at 100k req/min.
- Integration tests with metrics pipeline validate at least 1s propagation latency for experiment metrics.
design_summary:
We will implement a central Experiment Runner service that owns state for active experiments, cohort allocations, and sequential checks. Key concepts: cohorts (static or dynamic), exposures (hard split vs. shadow), checkers (frequentist sequential test + optional Bayesian posterior monitor), and actions (pause, rollback, promote). A canonical JSON experiment spec will be used by Console and the API. The runner emits decisions to the audit log and calls the routing control plane to update allocations.

Frontend: Console form + YAML editor, visual ramp timeline, and metric charts. Backend: lightweight coordinator w/ pluggable statistical adapters. Routing: an API to apply weighted allocations and shadow forwarding. Metrics: standardized metric names, guardrails config, and time-windowed evaluation.
statistical_checks:
Primary/Guardrail setup: users declare 1 primary metric and 0-N guardrail metrics. Each metric includes direction (higher/better), unit, and min-sample-size.

Sequential rules: default to an alpha-spending approach (O'Brien-Fleming style) with adjustable alpha (default 0.05). For customers preferring Bayesian checks, we support a conjugate beta/binomial or Gaussian model with posterior probability thresholds (default: 0.975 for win, <0.025 for loss).

Early-stop: if the sequential test crosses thresholds for win or loss at any interim check and sample constraints are satisfied, the runner will mark the experiment outcome.

Minimum effect/size: experiments must declare minimum detectable effect (MDE) or the runner will compute conservative MDE based on historical variance.

Multiple comparisons: when evaluating multiple cohorts or metrics, default correction is Bonferroni; advanced users can opt into hierarchical testing or false discovery rate (FDR) control.

Action hysteresis: to avoid flapping, auto-rollback requires the trigger condition to persist across X consecutive windows (configurable; default 3).
rollout_controls:
Exposure modes: canary (weighted traffic), stratified A/B (cohort splits), shadow (mirror requests), and staged ramp (time-based increases).

Ramping policy: user can define schedule points (e.g., 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with dwell times. Default schedule: 5% for 1h, 20% for 2h, 50% for 6h, 100% final.

Auto-rollback policies: numerical rules (e.g., primary metric drop >5% and p<0.01 OR Bayesian posterior of harm >0.9), availability/failure spikes (error rate >2% absolute increase over baseline), cost regressions (token cost per request >20% increase).

Manual override: operators can pause, reject, or force-promote experiments; actions are recorded in audit log.

Shadowing: when enabled, traffic is mirrored to candidate version; results are recorded but not returned to clients. Useful for validating latency/regressions without exposure.
infra_changes:
- New Experiment Runner microservice (state + scheduler).
- Routing control API extensions: applyExperimentAllocation(experiment_id, cohort, allocation) and setShadowTarget(...).
- Metric ingestion tags: experiments must be tagged at emission time (experiment_id, cohort_id).
- Console components: Create/Edit experiment UI, cohort builder, schedule editor, metric selector, and decision timeline.
- Rollback hooks: signer service to execute safe rollbacks with idempotency.
- Audit storage: append-only experiment audit stream stored in object store/DB for compliance.
metrics_integration:
Primary metrics: model quality (task-specific: BLEU, accuracy, rerank CTR), API-level: latency P50/P95, p99, error rate, token consumption per request, downstream business metrics (conversion).

Data pipeline: metrics annotated by experiment tags arrive to metrics ingestion (Prometheus + ingestion service) -> bucketing by window -> Experiment Runner pulls aggregated windows for checks.

SLO/thresholds: Runner uses rolling windows with configurable length (default 15m) and computes relative deltas and standardized effect sizes.
monitoring_playbook:
- On guardrail alert: Runner notifies experiment owner via Slack + Console banner and auto-pauses allocation.
- If auto-rollback triggered: routing layer reverts allocation to baseline and posts an incident ticket with audit details and PR suggestions.
- Post-incident: run an automated postmortem checklist: collect snapshots, recent model commits, input samples, and alert SRE to investigate infrastructure causes.
- Communication: template messages for customer-facing incidents and internal postmortem notes.
risks:
- False positives/negatives from incorrect statistical config could cause unnecessary rollbacks.
- Routing latency when applying allocations at large scale.
- Data tagging gaps causing incomplete metrics for checks.
- Cross-cohort contamination when cookies/IDs are not stable across clients.
- Compliance: audit trail must be tamper-evident for enterprise customers.
next_steps:
1) Finalize experiment spec JSON schema (PM + Eng review)
2) Prototype runner evaluating synthetic metrics for 2 weeks (Eng)
3) Console mockups and usability tests (Design)
4) Integrate with routing API and run internal dogfood experiments
5) Iterate on default statistical config based on real variance observed
6) Gradual opt-in with a small set of customers before GA
